_comment: vnflight game configuration. This ships with NO games attached — add your own. Each key under 'games' is a game id you choose. Entries whose key starts with an underscore are DISABLED documentation examples: copy one, remove the leading underscore, and edit the paths. See docs/USER.md (The config file) for every field.
_mods_manifest_comment: Optional. Path to a mods repository's manifest.json (absolute, or relative to this file; never a URL). A game entry WITHOUT a 'mods' key takes its adapters from the manifest entry for its id (or for the id named by its 'adapters' key), verified by sha256. An entry with a 'mods' list uses that list as written; an empty list means no adapters.

mods_snapshot._comment: The adapter snapshot this vnflight release was tested with. Used only by `fetch-mods` when it is run without a URL and --sha256 (it prints both and asks before downloading); nothing fetches it implicitly. Bump url and sha256 together when the mods repository is updated.

games._comment: No games are configured out of the box. Copy an example below, drop the leading underscore, and point the paths at a game you own. See docs/USER.md.

_example_local_renpy_game._comment: A locally owned Ren'Py game launched directly through a Ren'Py SDK you supply. 'launch' is the command to start it (SDK executable + game project dir); paths are relative to this vnflight.json (absolute paths also work).
_example_local_renpy_game.name: My Visual Novel

_example_sample_game_repo._comment: Wiring one of the self-made sample games (its own repo). Clone the sample-game repo (e.g. 'echoes_of_tomorrow') and the 'mods' repo, point 'launch' at your Ren'Py SDK + the cloned game dir, and set 'mods_manifest' above to the mods repo's manifest.json: this entry has no 'mods' key, so its adapters come from the manifest entry for its id.
_example_sample_game_repo.name: Echoes of Tomorrow

_example_steam_game._comment: A commercial game you own on Steam, launched via its store URL. 'game_dir' tells vnflight where the installed game lives so install-shim can patch it; launcher-mediated launches are handled automatically via the launch-file handshake. Compatibility adapters live in the separate mods repo; point mods_manifest at its manifest.json (see docs/USER.md, Mods).
_example_steam_game.name: Doki Doki Literature Club

_example_gog_game._comment: A commercial game you own on GOG, launched via GOG Galaxy. See the mods repo README before enabling a commercial-game adapter.
_example_gog_game.name: Roadwarden
